title: Frequently Asked Questions
subtitle: Everything you need to know about ACIKY, our classes and Kundalini Yoga

cat1.title: About ACIKY
cat1.a1: ACIKY is the Cuban Alliance of Kundalini Yoga Instructors, an organization that brings together KRI-certified instructors in Cuba to organize, strengthen and expand the practice of Kundalini Yoga across the island.
cat1.a2: It's an ancient practice that combines physical postures (kriyas), breathing techniques (pranayama), meditation and mantras to awaken vital energy and elevate consciousness, reducing stress and promoting greater balance and purpose.
cat1.q3: Who taught this lineage of Kundalini Yoga?
cat1.a3: ACIKY teaches Kundalini Yoga as transmitted by Master Yogi Bhajan (1929–2004), who brought this tradition from East to West in 1969.
cat1.q4: Does ACIKY have a single leader?
cat1.a4: No. Decisions are made collectively through a Steering Committee, without a single leadership figure.
cat1.q5: Which organizations does ACIKY collaborate with?
cat1.a5: Its alliances include Casa de Asia, the Office of the Historian of Havana, the Embassy of India in Cuba, IKYTA (International Kundalini Yoga Teachers Association), 3HO, and several schools and related spaces in Cuba and the region.
cat1.q6: In which Cuban provinces does ACIKY have a presence?
cat1.a6: ACIKY currently has a presence in 3 provinces and is actively working to expand to all 15 provinces of the country through the Golden Routes project.

cat2.title: Classes and in-person practice
cat2.q1: How can I see the class schedule?
cat2.a1: The "Classes" section of the site publishes the updated weekly schedule.
cat2.a2: In-person classes and meditations take place at spaces like Casa Museo de Asia, among other practice locations ACIKY keeps adding across Cuba.
cat2.a3: Yes, ACIKY offers a free first class so new participants can try the practice with no commitment.
cat2.q4: What should I bring to class?
cat2.a4: It's recommended to arrive 10 minutes early, wear comfortable clothing, bring a blanket, and avoid eating for 2 hours before practice.
cat2.q5: Do I need to reserve my spot?
cat2.a5: Yes, it's recommended to confirm your reservation via WhatsApp before attending.
cat2.a6: Yes, classes are designed for all levels, from beginners to more advanced practitioners.

cat3.title: Online Sadhanas (daily virtual practice)
cat3.a1: It's a daily spiritual practice held during the Ambrosial Hours — or Amrit Vela, "the nectar time" — the periods from 4:00 to 7:00 AM and 4:00 to 7:00 PM, when energy is calmest and most receptive. ACIKY offers it virtually to connect the community regardless of location.
cat3.q2: On which platform are sadhanas held?
cat3.q3: How do I join the Online Sadhanas?
cat3.a3: You need to contact ACIKY (via WhatsApp) to receive the access link for the daily sessions.
cat3.q4: What do I need to participate?
cat3.a4: A device with a stable internet connection, clear audio (headphones or speakers), and keeping your microphone muted during the session to preserve the collective atmosphere.
cat3.q5: What is the structure of a sadhana?
cat3.a5: It follows the traditional sequence: Japji Sahib, opening, warm-up, kriya, meditation, and closing prayer.
cat3.q6: Is there a recommended minimum commitment?
cat3.a6: Yes, it's suggested to commit initially to 40 consecutive days to build the habit and experience the full benefits of the practice.
cat3.q7: Can I start little by little?
cat3.a7: Yes, newcomers are encouraged to first join Sunday sessions and gradually add more days over time.

cat4.title: Golden Routes (national expansion)
cat4.a1: It's ACIKY's expansion project that brings Kundalini Yoga to communities across all of Cuba's provinces, through certified instructors who travel to teach and drive local practice groups.
cat4.a2: It consists of six stages: identifying the need, planning the route, travel and immersion, intensive teaching, establishing a local group, and ongoing follow-up.
cat4.q3: How can I take part in the Golden Routes?
cat4.a3: There are four ways to get involved: as a traveling instructor (KRI certification, at least 1 year of experience and availability to travel), local host (offering space, coordinating participants or supporting with lodging), emerging leader (receiving free training to sustain the practice in their community), or sponsor (financially supporting transportation, materials or equipment).
cat4.q4: What is the goal of the Golden Routes?
cat4.a4: To complete coverage of all 15 Cuban provinces by 2026 and consolidate a self-sustaining network with local instructors by 2027.

cat5.title: Rebirthing Ceremonies
cat5.a1: It's a transformative experience that symbolizes the "death" of the limited ego and the birth of an expanded consciousness, using breathwork (pranayama), mantras, meditation and a symbolic release process ("transforming fire").
cat5.q2: Who is this experience designed for?
cat5.a2: For people going through life transitions, those seeking to heal emotional or family patterns, those seeking clearer purpose, and generally any spiritual seeker committed to their growth.
cat5.q3: How do I find out about upcoming dates?
cat5.a3: Upcoming ceremonies are announced in the corresponding section of the site; availability can also be checked directly via WhatsApp.

cat6.title: Faro de Luz Festival
cat6.q1: What is the Faro de Luz Festival?
cat6.a1: It's ACIKY's annual yoga and wellness event. For dates, venue and details of the current edition, check the festival page, since this information is updated every year.

cat7.title: Membership for instructors
cat7.q1: Who can become an ACIKY member?
cat7.a1: ACIKY accepts as members Kundalini Yoga instructors with KRI (Kundalini Research Institute) certification.
cat7.q2: How do I join as a certified instructor?
cat7.a2: Write to ACIKY via WhatsApp or email to start the membership process. You can also check the membership guide available on the site.
cat7.q3: What does participating as a member involve?
cat7.a3: Members participate in different ways: organizing activities, leading classes, serving the community, attending events, promoting the practice, and exchanging ideas within the collective.
cat7.q4: What if I don't have KRI certification yet but want to teach someday?
cat7.a4: ACIKY guides those who feel called to train as instructors on the path to KRI certification; it's recommended to contact us directly for more information.
cat7.q5: Does ACIKY have an evaluation or professional development team?
cat7.a5: Yes, it has a CEU Evaluation Team focused on training and teaching, service (seva) and leadership, research, and additional benefits for instructors.

cat8.title: Donations and support
cat8.q1: How can I support ACIKY financially?
cat8.a1: Through the donations section of the site, which explains how to help Kundalini Yoga keep reaching more people in Cuba.

cat9.title: Contact and account
cat9.a1: Via WhatsApp (+53 5075-9360), through the site's contact form, or through social media (Facebook and Instagram @acikycuba).
cat9.q2: Do I need to create an account to participate?
cat9.a2: The site allows you to sign in or register to access a personal profile, though booking your free first class or joining sadhanas only requires writing via WhatsApp.
cat9.a3: Yes: Facebook, Instagram (@acikycuba) and WhatsApp, all linked in the site's footer.

ctaText: Write to us and we'll help you directly.
